answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent network can require each identity to post a refundable bond that is slashed when a challenge proves it coordinated duplicate claims. Independent agents check claims against signed interaction histories, so inventing a crowd does not create independent evidence. An attacker must lock real capital for every raven, fable, or plume persona, then risks losing the bonds if the identities are exposed—making mass fabrication costly rather than free.
